qualifiedNameTokens` declaration, the `packParent.getParent() != null` package-walk check, and the `for (String token : qualifiedNameTokens)` matching loop) to see

which commit last produced that code.

**(2) The change that introduced the bug**

The fix (`c0716524`) corrects two things:
- The package-name-walking check `packParent.getParent() != null` (should st

op at the top-level/default package).
- The core matching logic: iterating over **all** tokens in an unordered `Set<String> qualifiedNameTokens` (which mixes the
referenced field/method's simple name, its declaring type's simple name, *and every package-name segment*) and testing each one for a name collision,

instead of only checking the relevant (last) token.

That "check every qualified-name token, including package segments, against locally-visible field/method/vari

is comparatively harmless (worst case: an extra, syntactically valid class import).

`adb2fd742` is the commit that ext
ended this same flawed matching pattern to a brand-new feature: **static field and method imports** (`addFieldImport`/`addMethodImport`). This is the commit that made it
possible to emit `import static ...Class.FIELD;` statements at all, and it reused the pre-existing (already imprecise) "match any
qualified-name token, including package segments" logic to decide whether a static import should be added. Because a package-name segment (e.g. `digest`) can coincidentally equal a method

not touch the `packParent.getParent()` line at all.

**(3) Supporting evidence**

- `git blame` on the pre-fix file shows the `packParent.getParent() != null` line and

`CtExecutableReference`/`CtFieldReference`-based static import support.
- Before `adb2fd742`, there was no `addFieldImport`/`addMethodImport` override at all — static im

## Bug-Introducing Commits
BIC: adb2fd7420b3bf01e696be87f4791759bfb6de53

## Reasoning

**(1) Investigation process**

I traced the history of `src/main/java/spoon/reflect/visitor/MinimalImportScanner.java` (the only source file touched by the fix, besides new tests) with `git log --follow` and found four commits that modified it prior to the fix:
- `a94e255b6` – created the file (fully-qualified type import fix)
- `adb2fd742` – "feature: allow spoon to do static imports for methods and fields (#1040)"
- `92a240ff` – "fix(imports): fix regressions with static imports and inner classes or enums (#1048)"
- `7b120441` – "fix(importscanner): fix regression in fuly-qualified mode (#1052)"

I then ran `git blame` on the pre-fix version (`946abfec`) of the exact lines touched by the fix (the `Set<String> qualifiedNameTokens` declaration, the `packParent.getParent() != null` package-walk check, and the `for (String token : qualifiedNameTokens)` matching loop) to see which commit last produced that code.

**(2) The change that introduced the bug**

The fix (`c0716524`) corrects two things:
- The package-name-walking check `packParent.getParent() != null` (should stop at the top-level/default package).
- The core matching logic: iterating over **all** tokens in an unordered `Set<String> qualifiedNameTokens` (which mixes the referenced field/method's simple name, its declaring type's simple name, *and every package-name segment*) and testing each one for a name collision, instead of only checking the relevant (last) token.

That "check every qualified-name token, including package segments, against locally-visible field/method/variable names" design already existed in `a94e255b6`, but at that point it only governed ordinary **class** imports — over-matching there is comparatively harmless (worst case: an extra, syntactically valid class import).

`adb2fd742` is the commit that extended this same flawed matching pattern to a brand-new feature: **static field and method imports** (`addFieldImport`/`addMethodImport`). This is the commit that made it possible to emit `import static ...Class.FIELD;` statements at all, and it reused the pre-existing (already imprecise) "match any qualified-name token, including package segments" logic to decide whether a static import should be added. Because a package-name segment (e.g. `digest`) can coincidentally equal a method name declared in the very class being processed (`DigestUtil.digest(...)`), the scanner produces a false-positive match and incorrectly emits a static import for a field (`STREAM_BUFFER_LENGTH`) that is already directly accessible in its own class — exactly the bug demonstrated by the new `DigestUtil`/`MessageDigest` test fixtures.

Subsequent commits `92a240ff` and `7b120441` refactored surrounding code (renaming `namedElements` to `fieldAndMethodsNames`/`localVariablesOfBlock`, adding local-variable detection) but preserved the same "iterate over the whole token set" flaw introduced in `adb2fd742`; they did not touch the `packParent.getParent()` line at all.

**(3) Supporting evidence**

- `git blame` on the pre-fix file shows the `packParent.getParent() != null` line and the `for (String token : qualifiedNameTokens) { ... }` structure both trace back to `adb2fd742`'s diff, where the method was substantially rewritten to add `CtExecutableReference`/`CtFieldReference`-based static import support.
- Before `adb2fd742`, there was no `addFieldImport`/`addMethodImport` override at all — static imports were not generated, so the specific bug (spurious `import static ...STREAM_BUFFER_LENGTH;`) could not have manifested earlier.
- `7b120441` only renamed variables and added local-variable lookup; it reused the same problematic `Set`+"check every token" approach without altering its faulty semantics, so it is a carrier of the bug rather than its origin.

**Uncertainty:** The specific matching pattern (checking every token in an unordered set) has roots even earlier, in the file's original creation (`a94e255b6`), for plain class imports. I'm treating `adb2fd742` as the primary bug-introducing commit because it is the point where this flawed pattern was actually wired into the static-field/method-import feature that the fix's test directly exercises — but if the intended "bug" is defined more broadly as "any commit that ever contained this token-matching flaw," `a94e255b6` and `7b120441` could also be considered contributing commits.
